newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean students bust blockade, seize police.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean students bust blockade, seize police.

text.p: Militant South Korean students seized about 10 riot policemen during fierce clashes outside a Seoul university on Monday, and one witness said a number of other police appeared to be badly injured.
The injuries occurred as student marchers burst through a police blockade of Hanyang University, Reuter photographer Yun Suk-bong said.
"A lot of policemen are lying on the street, and they seem badly hurt," he said.
Officers were sprawled helplessly on the ground, their steel helmets scattered around them. Students appeared to be trying to revive one motionless officer.
Yun said students had seized about 10 officers and were holding them outside the college gates where some 3,000 students were massing.
Many of the students were armed with metal pipes and crude petrol bombs fashioned from beer bottles.
Other witnesses said around 8,000 students were in and around the campus on the fourth day of protests in Seoul to demand the resignation of President Kim Young-sam.
One group of students attacked an armoured police teargas launcher with metal pipes, smashing its windows and pounding its black metal sides.
Yun said one young riot officer lying on the ground with an injured leg begged students for help.
Several policemen had their clothes set on fire by Molotov cocktails.
At least two police officers tried to escape the fighting by dashing inside the campus, Yun said.

Prosecutors on Monday vowed to "deal sternly" with the violence, which has been orchestrated by an outlawed student body, the Hanchongryon, which the government maintains is a stooge of rival North Korea.
As many as 10,000 students took to the streets of Seoul over the weekend, dashing through the city's subway system and emerging suddenly at station entrances to engage police.
The violence was sparked by Kim's refusal to bow to opposition demands and reveal how much he spent on his 1992 election campaign.
Allegations that Kim grossly overspent have surfaced in the final year of his presidency in the wake of a corruption scandal involving loans to bankrupt Hanbo Steel.
The scandal has led to the arrest of Kim's son and several of his closest aides, shattering his credibility.
